# Certificates and Quorum Logic

TinyBFT collects matching messages from replicas into *quorum certificates*. Three
certificate flavours are defined — Prepare, Commit, and Checkpoint — but they all
share the same shape and algorithm, generated from a single X-macro. A separate
*prepared certificate* combines a Pre_prepare with a Prepare certificate. The
quorum logic lives entirely in `src/tbft_certificate.c` (`tbft_certificate.c:1`).

## Overview

A *quorum certificate* is a per-sequence-number object that records one
contribution per replica id, groups contributions by the digest of the
message they carry, and signals "complete" once a single digest accumulates
`2f+1` matching contributions. Three flavours exist:

| Flavour | Type | Carries | Complete condition |
|---|---|---|---|
| Prepare | `tbft_prepare_cert_t` | `<view, seqno, digest, …>` | `2f` matching prepares for a seqno |
| Commit | `tbft_commit_cert_t` | `<view, seqno, digest, …>` | `2f+1` matching commits for a seqno |
| Checkpoint | `tbft_checkpoint_cert_t` | `<seqno, digest, …>` | `2f+1` matching checkpoints for a seqno |
| Prepared | `tbft_prepared_cert_t` | one Pre_prepare + a `tbft_prepare_cert_t` | PP stored + 2f matching Prepares + digests match |

All three flavours are produced by a single X-macro `CERT_IMPL` instantiated
three times in `tbft_certificate.c:163-165`. The only differences between
the instantiations are:

1. The slot size (Commit / Prepare / Checkpoint have different fixed
   rep headers, so the maximum bytes per entry differ).
2. The offset of the digest within the message body (Prepare and Commit
   carry view+seqno before the digest, while Checkpoint carries only
   seqno).
3. The expected `tbft_msg_tag_t`.

`tbft_prepared_cert_t` is the only certificate that owns a Pre_prepare
message — it is described separately in
[Prepared certificate](#prepared-certificate-tbft_prepared_cert_t--its-special-role).

## `CERT_IMPL` macro (X-macro pattern)

The macro is defined at `tbft_certificate.c:36` and expanded three times
near the bottom of the same file:

```c
CERT_IMPL(tbft_commit_cert,     tbft_commit_cert_t,     TBFT_CERT_COMMIT_MSG_SIZE,     COMMIT_DIGEST_OFFSET,     TBFT_MSG_COMMIT)        // tbft_certificate.c:163
CERT_IMPL(tbft_checkpoint_cert, tbft_checkpoint_cert_t, TBFT_CERT_CHECKPOINT_MSG_SIZE, CHECKPOINT_DIGEST_OFFSET, TBFT_MSG_CHECKPOINT)   // tbft_certificate.c:164
CERT_IMPL(tbft_prepare_cert,    tbft_prepare_cert_t,    TBFT_CERT_PREPARE_MSG_SIZE,    PREPARE_DIGEST_OFFSET,    TBFT_MSG_PREPARE)       // tbft_certificate.c:165
```

Each expansion generates six functions with the prefix substituted in:

| Generated function | Macro emission |
|---|---|
| `tbft_<prefix>_init` | sets `mym_idx = -1`, threshold, zero |
| `tbft_<prefix>_clear` | preserves threshold, zeroes the rest |
| `tbft_<prefix>_add` | adds a remote replica's message (deduplicates per sender) |
| `tbft_<prefix>_add_mine` | adds the local node's own message |
| `tbft_<prefix>_cvalue` | returns the winning message bytes (`correct[i] >= threshold`) |
| `tbft_<prefix>_is_complete` | shorthand for `cvalue() != NULL` |

The pattern guarantees that the three certificate types can never drift
out of sync — every fix to the algorithm is applied identically to all
three at the macro-expansion site.

### Digest extraction

The macro takes a `digest_offset` argument and an `expected_tag`. The
helper `extract_msg_digest` (`tbft_certificate.c:19-34`) does the
extraction, length, and tag checks in one place. The offsets are
defined just above the macro instantiations:

| Message | Digest offset | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Prepare | `sizeof(hdr) + sizeof(view) + sizeof(seqno)` | `tbft_certificate.c:159` |
| Commit | `sizeof(hdr) + sizeof(view) + sizeof(seqno)` | `tbft_certificate.c:160` |
| Checkpoint | `sizeof(hdr) + sizeof(seqno)` | `tbft_certificate.c:161` |

The macros therefore compare *only the digest portion* of each message
when grouping, not the entire rep struct (which would include the
sender-specific `id` field and per-sender authenticator). The
comment at `tbft_certificate.c:11-15` calls this a "CRITICAL FIX".

## Generated struct layout (`TBFT_CERT_DECLARE`)

The struct template is defined at `tbft_certificate.h:42-51` and
instantiated three times at `tbft_certificate.h:53-55`:

```c
#define TBFT_CERT_DECLARE(name, msg_size)                                      \
typedef struct {                                                               \
    tbft_bitmap_t  bmap;              /* which sender IDs have contributed */  \
    tbft_digest_t  val_digests[TBFT_CERT_MAX_VALS];                            \
    uint8_t        vals[TBFT_CERT_MAX_VALS][(msg_size)];                       \
    int            correct[TBFT_CERT_MAX_VALS];                                \
    int            num_vals;                                                   \
    int            mym_idx;                                                    \
    int            complete_threshold;                                          \
} name

TBFT_CERT_DECLARE(tbft_commit_cert_t,     TBFT_CERT_COMMIT_MSG_SIZE);
TBFT_CERT_DECLARE(tbft_checkpoint_cert_t, TBFT_CERT_CHECKPOINT_MSG_SIZE);
TBFT_CERT_DECLARE(tbft_prepare_cert_t,    TBFT_CERT_PREPARE_MSG_SIZE);
```

### Field semantics

| Field | Type | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `bmap` | `tbft_bitmap_t` | One bit per replica id. A set bit means "this sender has already contributed to some digest group". |
| `val_digests[]` | `tbft_digest_t[TBFT_CERT_MAX_VALS]` | One SHA-256 digest per distinct value seen. Used for fast equality comparison. |
| `vals[][]` | `uint8_t[TBFT_CERT_MAX_VALS][msg_size]` | The full stored message bytes for retrieval by `cvalue()`. |
| `correct[]` | `int[TBFT_CERT_MAX_VALS]` | Counter of how many senders agree on this value. |
| `num_vals` | `int` | Number of distinct digest groups currently stored. Bounded by `TBFT_CERT_MAX_VALS`. |
| `mym_idx` | `int` | Index of the slot holding the local replica's own message; `-1` if we have not voted. |
| `complete_threshold` | `int` | Required matching contributions to declare quorum (`2f+1` for Commit/Checkpoint, `2f` for Prepare). |

### Per-flavour slot size

The slot-size macros at `tbft_certificate.h:28-35` are the maximum
across the three rep types plus `TBFT_AUTH_SIZE`:

| Flavour | `TBFT_CERT_*_MSG_SIZE` formula |
|---|---|
| Commit | `sizeof(tbft_commit_rep_t) + TBFT_AUTH_SIZE` |
| Checkpoint | `sizeof(tbft_checkpoint_rep_t) + TBFT_AUTH_SIZE` |
| Prepare | `sizeof(tbft_prepare_rep_t) + TBFT_AUTH_SIZE` |

The largest of these sizes dominates `vals[][]` for a given
configuration; the macro is instantiated for each flavour with its own
size so each cert is sized for what it actually stores.

## Bitmap (`tbft_bitmap_t` = `uint64_t`)

The bitmap is a `uint64_t` typedef'd at `tbft_types.h:103`. Each
certificate carries exactly one bitmap, and a set bit at position `i`
means "replica `i` has already contributed to this cert". Operations
are provided at `tbft_types.h:105-130`:

| Function | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `tbft_bitmap_set` | Set bit `i` |
| `tbft_bitmap_clear` | Clear bit `i` |
| `tbft_bitmap_test` | Read bit `i` |
| `tbft_bitmap_zero` | Clear all bits |
| `tbft_bitmap_count` | Population count (`__builtin_popcountll`) |

Because the bitmap is a single `uint64_t`, the hard upper bound is 64
senders — this is enforced by `_Static_assert(TBFT_MAX_NUM_REPLICAS <= 64)`
in `tbft_config.h`. The check `sender_id < 0 || sender_id >= 64` is
duplicated inside the macro body at `tbft_certificate.c:56` and `:97`
to reject out-of-range ids without touching the bitmap.

The bitmap serves three purposes:

1. **Duplicate-sender guard**: a second message from the same sender
   for the same seqno is silently dropped (`tbft_certificate.c:60-62`).
2. **Anti-replay**: a captured Prepare/Commit cannot be replayed
   against the same seqno because the sender bit is already set.
3. **Vote accounting**: the sum of the bits equals the total number
   of distinct senders that have contributed.

## Algorithm: add a value, check threshold, detect complete

The hot path inside `tbft_<prefix>_add` (`tbft_certificate.c:53-92`)
executes the following steps:

1. **Range guard** — `sender_id` must be in `[0, 64)`. `msg_len` must
   be positive and `<= msg_slot_size`. Negative or oversized messages
   are rejected with no truncation (`tbft_certificate.c:56-58`).
2. **Duplicate guard** — if the sender's bit is already set in
   `bmap`, the message is dropped (`tbft_certificate.c:60-62`).
3. **Digest extraction** — `extract_msg_digest` (line 19) returns
   `NULL` if the body is too short, the tag does not match, or the
   pointer is bad.
4. **Match against existing digests** — iterate the stored
   `val_digests[0..num_vals-1]`. On the first digest match (via
   `tbft_digest_equal`), set the sender bit and increment
   `correct[i]`, then return. This is the "same value" path.
5. **New distinct value** — if no existing digest matched, the
   candidate is stored as a new group provided `num_vals <
   TBFT_CERT_MAX_VALS`. The full message bytes are copied into
   `vals[num_vals]` and the digest into `val_digests[num_vals]`,
   `correct[num_vals] = 1`, `bmap` bit set, `num_vals++`.
6. **Capacity exhaustion** — if `num_vals >= TBFT_CERT_MAX_VALS`, the
   new value is rejected with no rollback. Beyond `f+1` distinct
   values a quorum of one value is guaranteed (by pigeonhole on
   `2f+1` matching contributions) so storing more is unnecessary.

`tbft_<prefix>_add_mine` (line 94-137) follows the same pattern but
treats the local replica specially: it sets `mym_idx` to the index of
the matching or newly-stored value, which lets the caller recover
its own message via `vals[pc.mym_idx]`. The "capacity exhaustion"
branch at line 128-134 deliberately does **not** set the bitmap bit
when storage fails — a marked-but-absent vote would corrupt
`cvalue()` recovery.

```text
+---------------------+
| sender_id range?    |--no--> reject
+---------------------+
         | yes
         v
+---------------------+
| msg_len valid?      |--no--> reject
+---------------------+
         | yes
         v
+---------------------+
| already voted?      |--yes-> reject (bmap test)
+---------------------+
         | no
         v
+---------------------+
| extract digest      |--NULL-> reject
+---------------------+
         | ok
         v
+---------------------+
| match any stored    |--yes-> inc correct[i], set bmap
| digest?             |        return
+---------------------+
         | no
         v
+---------------------+
| num_vals < f+1 ?    |--no--> reject (pigeonhole)
+---------------------+
         | yes
         v
   store vals[], val_digests[], correct=1, set bmap, num_vals++
```

### Completion detection

`tbft_<prefix>_cvalue` (`tbft_certificate.c:139-147`) walks
`correct[0..num_vals-1]` and returns the message bytes for the first
slot whose counter is at least `complete_threshold`. `is_complete` is
a one-liner that calls `cvalue`. Because `cvalue` is linear in
`num_vals` (≤ `f+1`), quorum detection is `O(f)` per call — cheap
enough to invoke on every incoming message.

## Threshold formulas

| Quantity | Formula | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| `TBFT_MAX_FAULTY` (`f`) | `(n - 1) / 3` | Standard BFT: at most `f` Byzantine replicas, `n ≥ 3f+1`. |
| `TBFT_CERT_MAX_VALS` | `f + 1` | Max distinct values stored per cert — once a replica observes `f+1` distinct digests, the pigeonhole principle guarantees a quorum for one of them. |
| Prepare quorum | `2f` | Pre_prepare (the primary's) + `2f` Prepares = `2f+1` matching prepare-class evidence. Configured as `ar->prepare_threshold` at `tbft_agreement_region.c:11`. |
| Commit quorum | `2f+1` | Standard intersection-with-intersection quorum; needed to commit. Configured as `ar->commit_threshold` at `tbft_agreement_region.c:12`. |
| Checkpoint quorum | `2f+1` | Stable checkpoint requires `2f+1` matching checkpoint messages. |
| View-change quorum | `2f+1` | Collected in `tbft_view_info_t::threshold`. |
| New-view proof | `f + 1` matching VCs | Each prepared proof in a New_view must appear in at least `f+1` of the collected View_change messages. Enforced at `tbft_view_info.c:182`. |

The Prepare threshold is lower than Commit/Checkpoint because the
primary's Pre_prepare counts as the `+1`, so a replica needs only `2f`
Prepares to know a request was prepared in the previous view.

## Standalone logs: `tbft_plog_t`, `tbft_clog_t`, `tbft_elog_t`

The original `Log<T>` template instantiations — `tbft_plog_t`
(Prepared log), `tbft_clog_t` (Commit log), `tbft_elog_t`
(Execution log) — were defined in `src/tbft_log.h` and
`src/tbft_prepared_cert.h`. They have been **superseded** by the
static memory regions and are no longer compiled into the build. The
header files contain an explicit note:

```c
/* NOTE: The original Log<T> types (tbft_plog_t, tbft_clog_t, tbft_elog_t)
 * defined in this file were superseded by the static memory regions:
 *   - tbft_agreement_region_t  (replaces plog — Pre_prepare/Prepare certs)
 *   - tbft_checkpoint_region_t (replaces clog + elog — Commit/Checkpoint)
 *   - tbft_special_region_t    (view-change, request queues)
 *                                                                tbft_log.h:9
 */
```

The function-level note in `tbft_prepared_cert.h:91-95` adds:

> `tbft_plog_t` (Log<Prepared_cert>) was superseded by
> `tbft_agreement_region_t` which serves the same purpose with better
> memory layout. The plog type and its functions are no longer used.

The corresponding `tbft_plog_init` and `tbft_plog_truncate`
implementations in `tbft_prepared_cert.c:92-95` are gone; only the
comment remains. This is a deliberate reduction in surface area, not
a missing feature — the static regions serve every purpose the old
logs covered, but with contiguous allocation and no per-message
malloc.

| Old name | Replacement | Location of replacement |
|---|---|---|
| `tbft_plog_t` (Log<Prepared_cert>) | `tbft_agreement_region_t` | `src/tbft_agreement_region.h:30` |
| `tbft_clog_t` (Log<Commit_cert>) | `tbft_checkpoint_region_t` (commit slots) | `src/tbft_checkpoint_region.h` |
| `tbft_elog_t` (Log<Execution>) | `tbft_checkpoint_region_t` (execution slots) | `src/tbft_checkpoint_region.h` |

## Prepared certificate (`tbft_prepared_cert_t`) — its special role

The prepared certificate is the only certificate in the system that
carries a Pre_prepare. Its struct is defined at
`tbft_prepared_cert.h:20-30`:

```c
typedef struct tbft_prepared_cert {
    uint8_t  pp_buf[TBFT_PP_MAX_SIZE];   // full Pre_prepare bytes
    int      pp_len;                     // 0 = no PP stored
    tbft_prepare_cert_t  pc;             // Prepare cert (2f required)
    int64_t  t_sent_us;                  // when the PP was stored
} tbft_prepared_cert_t;
```

`TBFT_PP_MAX_SIZE` is `TBFT_MAX_MESSAGE_SIZE` (`tbft_prepared_cert.h:18`),
so the slot can hold a maximum-size Pre_prepare.

### Completion semantics

`tbft_prepared_cert_is_complete` (`tbft_prepared_cert.c:76-90`) is the
guard for transitioning from "prepared" to "committed-local":

```c
bool tbft_prepared_cert_is_complete(const tbft_prepared_cert_t *cert) {
    if (cert->pp_len == 0) return false;                                 // :78
    if (!tbft_prepare_cert_is_complete(&cert->pc)) return false;        // :79

    const uint8_t *pval = tbft_prepare_cert_cvalue(&cert->pc);          // :82
    if (!pval) return false;

    const tbft_pre_prepare_rep_t *pp = (const tbft_pre_prepare_rep_t *)cert->pp_buf;
    const tbft_prepare_rep_t *prep    = (const tbft_prepare_rep_t *)pval;
    return tbft_digest_equal(&pp->digest, &prep->digest);                // :89
}
```

Three conditions must hold:

1. A Pre_prepare is present (`pp_len > 0`).
2. The Prepare cert inside it has reached its `2f` threshold.
3. The Pre_prepare's digest equals the digest of the winning Prepare
   group's message — this is what binds a primary's Pre_prepare to
   the matching set of Prepares.

### Pre_prepare storage rules

`tbft_prepared_cert_add_pp` (`tbft_prepared_cert.c:22-60`) implements
the PBFT rule for accepting a Pre_prepare:

| Existing PP state | Incoming PP | Action |
|---|---|---|
| none | any | store (`tbft_prepared_cert.c:56`) |
| present, **different seqno** | any | unconditional overwrite (the slot was recycled by window advance) |
| present, **same seqno, same digest, higher view** | any | overwrite (re-proposal in a new view) |
| present, **same seqno, same view, different digest** | any | reject (equivocation) |
| present, **same seqno, different digest** | any | reject |

The "different seqno ⇒ overwrite" branch is what makes the circular
window safe — when `tbft_ar_truncate` advances `head`, the slots
are cleared and a Pre_prepare for a future seqno is allowed to
overwrite stale contents.

### Accessors

Two static inlines at `tbft_prepared_cert.h:73-88` provide
type-checked access to the stored Pre_prepare:

| Function | Returns |
|---|---|
| `tbft_prepared_cert_pp` | raw `uint8_t *` |
| `tbft_prepared_cert_pp_rep` | typed `const tbft_pre_prepare_rep_t *` |

Both return `NULL` when `pp_len == 0`.

## Memory cost per cert

The cost of a single `tbft_<X>_cert_t` instance is:

```
sizeof(tbft_bitmap_t)               //  8 bytes  bmap
+ TBFT_CERT_MAX_VALS * 32           // 32 × (f+1) bytes  val_digests[]
+ TBFT_CERT_MAX_VALS * MSG_SIZE     // message-size × (f+1) bytes  vals[][]
+ TBFT_CERT_MAX_VALS * 4            // 4 × (f+1) bytes  correct[]
+ 3 * 4                             // 12 bytes  num_vals, mym_idx, complete_threshold
```

With default Kconfig (`n=4`, `f=1`, `MAX_MESSAGE_SIZE=2048`,
`CERT_MAX_VALS = f+1 = 2`):

| Component | Bytes |
|---|---|
| `bmap` | 8 |
| `val_digests[2]` | 64 |
| `vals[2][~80]` (Prepare: rep + auth) | ~160 |
| `vals[2][~80]` (Commit: rep + auth) | ~160 |
| `vals[2][~80]` (Checkpoint: rep + auth) | ~160 |
| `correct[2]` | 8 |
| counters | 12 |

The dominant cost is `vals[][]` — `(f+1) × max_msg_size`. With
`n=7`, `f=2`, `MAX_MESSAGE_SIZE=2048`: `3 × 2048 = 6 KiB` per cert
slot, and an agreement slice holds one prepared cert plus one commit
cert, so `~12 KiB` per slice, `~48 KiB` for a `WINDOW_SIZE=4`
region. This is why the static sizing guidelines in
`docs/AGENT.md` recommend `WINDOW_SIZE=4` for ESP32-C3.

The prepared certificate is much larger because `pp_buf` is sized to
`TBFT_MAX_MESSAGE_SIZE`:

```
sizeof(tbft_prepared_cert_t) ≈ pp_buf (MAX_MESSAGE_SIZE)
                              + pc (~few hundred bytes)
                              + 8 + 4
```

For `MAX_MESSAGE_SIZE=2048` this is just over 2 KiB. With
`WINDOW_SIZE=4` that is `~8 KiB` of Pre_prepare storage across the
agreement region — the main reason `MAX_MESSAGE_SIZE` is the primary
DRAM budget knob.
